column1: Table 22 | Escalation pathway for diuretic therapy in AKI-related volume overload in adults Step  Dose/administration  Monitoring/goal    Assessment  Furosemide 1.0 mg/kg (i.v. bolus). Use1.5mg/kg if patient was previously ondiuretics.  Goal: >200 ml urine output within 2hours. If met, continue scheduled dosinguntil target fluid removal achieved.    Escalation  If Step 1 fails, double the dose (e.g.,160–200 mg i.v. bolus) every 6–12hours.  Maximize bolus dose before switching toinfusion. Max bolus: 200 mg.    Synergism  Add a thiazide-like diuretic (e.g.,metolazone 5–10 mg p.o. orchlorothiazide 500 mg i.v.).  Administer 30–60 minutes before theloop diuretic to block distal sodiumreabsorption.    Intensify  Switch to continuous i.v. infusion.Start at 5-10mg/hr.  Titrate up to 20 mg/hr (more effective formaintaining steady-state natriuresis)    Failure  Re-evaluate for RRT.  If net negative balance is not achieveddespite max therapy or if K+/pH arederanged. AKI, acute kidney injury; i.v., intravenous; K, potassium; p.o., oral; RRT, renal replacement therapy
